stories.title: Apple is reportedly cutting budgets for its internal AI usage
stories.simple_summary: Apple is spending less money on artificial intelligence tools that help its own engineers do their jobs. This is a decision the company made internally about its own budgets.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and people who work at Apple. There's nothing you need to do as a customer or small business owner.

stories.title: After the midterms, a bigger clash over data centers could be coming
stories.simple_summary: People from both political parties are starting to oppose large data centers in their communities. Data centers are huge facilities that store information and power AI systems.
stories.why_it_matters: If data centers get blocked or restricted in your area, it could slow down how fast internet and AI services work for local businesses and residents.

stories.title: Star mathematician Ma Xiao leaves the US for China – and a career pivot to AI
stories.simple_summary: A famous mathematician from the United States has moved to China and is now focusing on artificial intelligence work instead of pure mathematics. This is mostly just career news about one person's choice.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to universities and technology researchers. There's nothing you need to do.

stories.title: NEWSLETTER: In midterm ballot measures, voters send a message to AI builders
stories.simple_summary: During recent elections, voters in multiple states sent messages about their concerns regarding AI through ballot measures and voting choices. People were expressing their views on how AI should be handled.
stories.why_it_matters: This shows that voters care about AI rules and safety. It could mean new laws about AI are coming to your state or community.

stories.title: AI PACs spent millions trying to shape Congress — here’s how they fared
stories.simple_summary: Companies in the AI industry spent millions of dollars trying to influence elections through political groups called PACs, with only mixed success in 2026. They are already planning to spend more money on the next election.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to people who follow politics and elections closely. For ordinary people, it means you may see more AI-related political ads in the future.

stories.title: Qualcomm is betting big on data centers as smartphone sales sink
stories.simple_summary: Qualcomm is a company that makes computer chips. Smartphone sales are dropping, so the company is moving its focus toward building powerful computers that run AI systems for companies like Amazon and Meta.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and tech professionals. It shows AI is becoming a bigger part of how technology companies make money.

stories.title: Nothing CEO says company’s mysterious AI-first device is dropping next month
stories.simple_summary: A phone company called Nothing says it will release a new device next month that uses AI to help you be more productive. The company has not yet explained exactly what this device will do.
stories.why_it_matters: If you like trying new phone technology, you might want to watch for this product. Most people will probably wait to see what it actually does before deciding whether to buy it.

stories.title: Almost no one uses AI agents to book their Uber, company says
stories.simple_summary: Uber says almost nobody is using AI assistants to book their rides. During a very busy week, only four people out of millions used this AI booking feature.
stories.why_it_matters: This shows that people still prefer booking rides the old way, by tapping buttons themselves. New AI features take time before people trust and use them.

stories.title: 17 better ways Elon Musk could have wasted $446 million
stories.simple_summary: This is a critical opinion article suggesting that someone spent a large amount of money in a wasteful way, possibly related to social media or internet activities. The article uses humor and complaints about social media.
stories.why_it_matters: This is opinion writing, not news about something that affects you. There's nothing you need to do.

stories.title: OpenAI is already trying to shape the 2028 election
stories.simple_summary: OpenAI, a major artificial intelligence company, is working to influence the presidential election in 2028. A leader at the company wants AI to be a central topic in that election and hopes it benefits both the country and OpenAI's business.
stories.why_it_matters: This shows that big AI companies are getting involved in politics. It means you should think carefully about AI policies and not just trust what these companies say is best.

stories.title: Arm Holdings Sales Climb 27% on AI Demand
stories.simple_summary: Arm Holdings, a company that designs computer chips, saw its sales go up by 27 percent because of increased demand for AI-related products. This is strong business growth.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and technology professionals. It shows the AI industry is growing quickly and companies are spending money on it.

stories.title: Google Tries to Walk Back Controversial School AI Policy Following Political Backlash
stories.simple_summary: Google tried to launch a policy about using AI in schools, but people complained about it. Now Google is backing away from that policy because of the complaints.
stories.why_it_matters: If you have children or grandchildren in school, you should pay attention to how schools use AI. Parents and communities can push back on policies they don't like.
